summary: ROTAR UY helps Uruguayan farmers choose what to plant next. It compares the farm's current rotation with three NASA-data-backed alternatives — each with why, evidence, benefits, gaps and risks — plus a sowing calendar, a 3D agro map down to 45 towns, a replay of the 2023 drought, a 10-year soil twin, a 200-mix priority explorer and a checkable 90-day action plan. Simplified soils map to Uruguay's official CONEAT groups (DGRN–MGAP), with a Soil Use and Management Plan reminder and INIA validation (guidance only, no official endorsement). It answers the Field Shift challenge: adapt farms with open NASA Earth observations, local soil and the farmer's own priorities.
details: What it does and how it works: ROTAR UY helps Uruguayan farmers choose what to plant next. Set department, soil, irrigation and priorities; it ranks 4 rotations on 6 axes (water, soil, erosion, income, forage, resilience) with an open 0–100 formula, plus a red-month calendar, 3D map, 2023-drought replay, 10-year soil twin, A/B duel with ±USD verdict and a checkable 90-day plan. Benefits: less bare soil, better water capture, diversified income, honest risks. Goal: a no-red-month calendar for every farm, starting with a 10-farm pilot with INIA. Single-file HTML/JS app using 9 NASA datasets, built with the free Perchance AI (Muse Spark); MGAP/CONEAT guidance; it supports, never replaces, agronomic judgment.
